title: Working at Redwood: Handbook, Roles, Benefits, Hiring & Tools
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview

This page is Redwood’s canonical employee handbook excerpt focused on what it means to work here, the role & career ladder framework, benefits and perks, an overview of the hiring & onboarding flow, and a concise internal tools guide for day‑to‑day productivity. Intended audience: all Redwood employees and new hires.

Purpose
- Single-source reference for people-ops, hiring managers, ICs, and new teammates.
- Clarify expectations for leveling and promotion.
- Surface benefits, policies, and practical links to tool-specific how‑tos.

1) Working at Redwood — values and ways of working

Introduction
Redwood is a developer-first, product-driven company focused on production-grade LLM inference. Our ways of working reflect that mission: shipping reliable software, instrumenting for measurable outcomes, and prioritizing operational excellence.

Core values (short):
- Customer-first engineering: measure impact in production.
- Ownership and clarity: clear ownership, decision records, and runbooks.
- Openness and continuous learning: share postmortems and write docs.
- Respectful collaboration: inclusive communication and psychological safety.

Working model
- Remote-first with hubs in SF and London. Expectation: overlap core hours (10:00–15:00 local) for collaboration.
- Flexible PTO: manager-approved time off with the expectation to coordinate on critical oncall or release windows.
- Asynchronous-first communication: prefer documented decisions in Confluence and tracking in Jira for cross-team work.

Communication norms
- Use Slack for fast coordination; Confluence for long-form documentation; Jira for tracked work.
- Decision records (ADRs) go in architecture-and-standards.
- All public-facing internal docs should include: purpose, owner, SLOs/metrics (if applicable), and rollback / contact information.

2) Roles and career ladders (overview)

Philosophy
- Role definitions prioritize impact, autonomy, and cross-functional influence. Promotion is evidence-based: documented outcomes, feedback, and calibration.

Primary career families
- Engineering (Backend, Runtime, Infra, SRE)
- Product (PM, Design, Research)
- Developer Experience & SDKs
- Applied ML / Model Onboarding & Evals
- Customer Success & Solutions
- Go-to-market (Sales, Growth, Marketing)
- People Ops & Finance/Legal

Leveling at-a-glance (applies across families)
- IC1 / Associate: entry-level contributors; focuses on delivery with guidance.
- IC2 / Mid: independent contributor; owns features, anticipates dependencies.
- IC3 / Senior: leads end-to-end projects, mentors others, influences design.
- IC4 / Staff: technical/functional leader; shapes strategy, leads cross-team initiatives.
- IC5+ / Principal / Director: company-scale impact, long-term strategy, external representation.

Promotion evidence checklist (what reviewers look for)
1. Impact metrics: shipped features, performance improvements, cost reductions, customer outcomes.
2. Scope growth: cross-team leadership, architectural influence, mentorship.
3. High-quality artifacts: PRs, design docs, ADRs, runbooks, postmortems.
4. Feedback: calibration from peers, managers, and stakeholders.

Role-specific guidance (examples)
- Serving Runtime Engineers: expected to lead kernel optimizations, perf regressions analysis, and release playbooks. Include profiling artifacts and benchmark dashboards as promotion evidence.
- Product Managers: expected to own metrics (latency, cost per token, quality regressions) and drive cross-functional rollouts.
- Applied ML Engineers: expected to maintain eval harnesses, regression sets, and quantization profiles with measured experiment results.

3) Benefits & perks (summary)

Health & financial benefits
- Medical/Dental/Vision: employer-sponsored plans with domestic and international options.
- 401(k) with company match (US) and local retirement plans in applicable regions.
- Equity: standard RSU/equity grants by hire band; refresh grants at promotional milestones.
- Competitive parental leave: primary and secondary caregiver policies.

Time off & well-being
- Flexible PTO and 12 company holidays + floating days.
- Stipend for mental health and coaching.
- Ergonomics / home office stipend on hire and refresh.

Learning & career support
- Annual learning stipend ($1,500 USD or local equivalent).
- Conference sponsorship and internal learning days.
- Mentorship program and regular career calibration sessions.

Perks & day-to-day support
- Remote-first allowances: home office, internet, and co-working stipend (where applicable).
- Commuter benefits for hub offices.
- Company retreat(s) annually (subject to health and budget).

How to access benefits
- Benefits enrollment and plan details live in the People Ops portal. New hires receive enrollment instructions during onboarding (see "New hire checklist" related page). For regional specifics, contact benefits@redwood.com.

4) Hiring & onboarding overview

Hiring principles
- Bias toward high-signal assessments: work samples and technical interviews that reflect the job.
- Consistent candidate experience: timely feedback, clear timelines, and transparent compensation bands.
- Diversity and inclusion: interview slates should include diverse representation and trained interviewers.

Typical hiring workflow
1. Requisition approved by hiring manager and finance.
2. Sourcing and outreach by Talent.
3. Phone screen (culture/role fit) + technical/assignment where applicable.
4. Onsite / virtual loop: 4–5 interviews + bar raiser.
5. Calibration and compensation committee review.
6. Offer, reference checks, and background check (where required).
7. Offer accepted → People Ops initiates onboarding.

New hire onboarding (first 90 days) — standard checklist
- Pre-day 1: equipment shipped, accounts provisioned (Okta/GSuite/Github), basic access to Confluence and Slack.
- Day 1: welcome orientation, People Ops benefits walkthrough, manager 1:1 to set expectations.
- Week 1: team onboarding sessions, reading list (architecture docs, runbooks), setting up dev environment.
- Month 1: first deliverable defined, buddy check-ins, security training completion.
- Month 3: performance check-in, career conversation, continued ramp goals.

Manager responsibilities for onboarding
- Create a 30/60/90 plan with clear milestones.
- Assign a peer buddy and schedule weekly 1:1s for the first 8 weeks.
- Ensure access to build/test infra and any customer sandboxes.

5) Internal tools guide (quick reference)

Authentication & access
- Okta is the single sign-on provider. Primary apps: GSuite, Github, Jira, Confluence, PagerDuty.
- Access requests: submit through the Access and Permissions page in Confluence or open a ticket with eng-infra access.

Code & CI/CD
- GitHub is the canonical code host. Repo naming convention: team-service or product-repo.
- CI: GitHub Actions and Jenkins for heavy pipeline tasks. See CI/CD runbooks for pipeline ownership.
- Release process: feature branches → PR → CI green → staged environment → canary → prod. Follow the release checklist in eng-platform/runbooks.

Issue tracking & planning
- Jira for delivery tracking. Epics map to quarterly objectives. Use labels: team, sprint, priority.

Monitoring & alerting
- Grafana dashboards for SLOs (latency p95, error-rate, cost per 1k tokens).
- Alerts routed to PagerDuty; oncall schedules in eng-sre/runbooks.
- Sentry for application errors; link errors to Jira tickets.

Documentation & knowledge sharing
- Confluence is the authoritative knowledge base. Use templates: design-spec, runbook, postmortem.
- Add owner and last-updated fields to every page. Tag pages with product or service labels for discoverability.

Customer & support tools
- Zendesk for support tickets, internal playbooks in customer-success-and-support.
- Integration guides for common customer setups live in that space.

Security & secrets
- Secrets should be stored in company-approved KMS/Hashi vaults. Avoid plaintext secrets in repos or Confluence.
- Security training mandatory in month 1. Incident reporting flows in security-and-compliance/incident-response-security.

6) Day-to-day procedures & quick links

Common quick tasks
- Request laptop replacement: People Ops > Equipment request form.
- File an access escalation: eng-infra > Access request template.
- Add a confluence page to team space: use the team page template.

Key links (internal)
- New hire checklist: /confluence/people-ops/new-hire-checklist
- Benefits portal: /confluence/people-ops/benefits-enrollment
- Career ladder docs: /confluence/company-handbook/company-handbook-roles-and-onboarding-2026
- Engineering runbooks: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks
- Oncall schedule & playbooks: /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks

7) Governance, ownership, and review cadence

Document ownership
- People Ops owns this handbook page; team owners own team-specific pages (eng, product, security).
- Each page must include: owner, reviewers, and last-updated date.

Review cadence
- People Ops: quarterly review of benefits & PTO policies.
- Eng leadership: quarterly review of career ladders and leveling guidance before company-wide calibration.
- Security & Compliance: annual review for policies requiring regulatory evidence.

8) FAQ (short)
- Q: How do I start a promotion case?
  A: Talk with your manager, gather artifacts (projects, metrics, feedback), and file a promotion packet three weeks before the next calibration cycle.
- Q: Who approves hiring?
  A: Hiring manager + finance + recruiting leadership must approve requisitions.
- Q: Where are runbooks for oncall?
  A: eng-sre/runbooks contains playbooks and escalation matrices.

Appendix: Templates and examples
- 30/60/90 new-hire template: available under People Ops templates.
- Promotion evidence checklist: available under company-handbook/roles-and-career-ladders.
- Oncall incident postmortem template: eng-sre/postmortem-template.

Contact
For questions about this handbook page or to request updates, contact people-ops@redwood.com or open a Confluence edit request and add the People Ops reviewer group.
